So he should have lost. The problem is that the Ottomates are really stupid, arrogant, and lazy. Pompei, General Pompei, is fighting for the Ottomans and he's going against Caesar. His strategy is really simple: Caesar has control over Italy, but it doesn't produce enough food. So all they need to do is lay siege to Italy, and if they start a war, it's over. That's all they have to do, right? We don't have to fight Caesar; just lay siege to Italy. The people will starve, rebel against Caesar, and he'll lose the war.

The problem is that the optimists are afraid that if Pompei wins the war, they would make him king, right? So what the optimists want to do is force both Pompei and Juju Caesar into a battle and kill them. This leads to something called the Battle of Farsus. At this time, Caesar needs to go fight Pompei, but Pompei doesn't have to fight Caesar; the ultimate forces him to fight in a battle called Farsus. Because Caesar has a loyal army, they defeat Pompei even though Pompei has more soldiers. Then Caesar will go conquer the entire Roman Empire and make himself dictator of Rome.

This leads to his assassination because the Romans are afraid he'll become king, abolish debts, reappropriate land, and give it to the people, making Rome a much more equal place. They killed him, leading to more civil war in which Octavius Caesar, Augustus Caesar, will be triumphant by inheriting Julius Caesar's army. At the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, he destroys Mark Anthony and Cleopatra, becoming the supreme ruler of the Roman Empire.

At this point in history, the problems of Rome don't really go away. He becomes emperor and during his time, things are stable. But after he dies, the Roman Empire goes back into civil war and keeps fighting until its collapse. What makes him emperor is that he takes Egypt and turns it into his private property, using the wealth to fund the army so all soldiers are loyal to him individually.

Augustus Caesar was not a military genius but appreciated that if the Roman people were to survive, they needed a culture as distinct and as powerful as Greek culture. The Greeks were culturally dominant at this time, and he feared that over time, all Romans would become Greeks. So he needs to create a culture distinct from the Greeks but considered more powerful than them. His main contribution is taking the work of Polybius, rewriting history from a Roman lens instead of a Greek one.

The book starts with the founding of Rome, where in Roman tradition, the Romans are descendants of Troy. The Trojans were destroyed by the Greeks through trickery and deception, leading to the Trojan horse. After that, the Greeks flood into the city and kill everyone, but there's a Trojan general named Inas and his wife Kisha.
